At this not-quite-bargain bin price and being light on content and mechanics, it feels like another VR gimmick that is only enjoyed for a few hours.  The only value proposition is 4 player coop shooter in a mildly MP starved VR market.

The negative that stands out most is the relative lack of player control features compared to other common VR games:
-You cannot adjust the aimpoint/tilt on the weapons to your specific VR grip.
-Like AZ Sunshine, no melee weapons (which are a general joy in VR zombie games).
-Difficulty/gun mechanics are balanced around reloading by simply putting the weapon to your ammo bag.  There is an advanced reloading option that you can use for your player, however, this will handicap you due to requiring both hands.  There's a small bonus to offset this, but it only increases materials gained instead of a bonus that offsets your effectiveness compared to someone using the arcade method of reload.
-Lack of character selection (you are randomly assigned a character look).

While less common, there are more advanced immersive features (arguably the strength of VR) that are also steadily showing up in other VR shooter games, but not found here:  
-No actual manipulation of your gear/rig (ie. pulling magazines out of specific ammo pouches instead of a single general pouch).
-No manipulation of backpack/dump pouch or other gear slots (aside from 2 inventory wrist slots).
-No slinging larger weapons over your shoulder/back.

This game, instead, pushes for the simplest arcade experience of VR shooters with little to no emphasis on immersion.  While this is fine for some players as a style choice, it seems like a game that ultimately has nothing new to offer in the VR market.  

The exception to this:  this does seem like there might be a challenge appeal to a 4 player friend group that wants to tackle the hardest difficulties.   The game also features a persistent MP lobby as the hub, theoretically making it easier to meet/coop with others if you lack the 3 other friends.  

If this is all you're after, then this game and price may be reasonable.  Otherwise, this game comes off as over-hyped and over-priced, downgraded for a casual occulus market.  Despite any issues I've had with SURV1V3, another VR MP zombie shooter -- (and there are issues), that game feels like a more fleshed out experience for nearly half the price.

I'm not sure if I can recommend it right now. While expectations for VR content should be different to that of regular games, £30 ($40) for 2-4 hours worth of content is a... questionable purchase, to say the least. I can only assume that you're supposed to replay missions ad nauseam.

I think the only reason I can think of to replay content is that there are floppy disks throughout the levels that you pick up and have to take to the end of the level in order to unlock attachments for the game's 6 guns. This is pretty much the only means of progression at the moment, as far as I can tell! Don't know about you, but a minor recoil reduction attachment in a VR game doesn't exactly seem worth grinding for. :) Also, those attachments can be, and often are, duplicates.

As other reviews have mentioned, matchmaking can be irritating at times. The bots in the game are a no-go, so you borderline have to matchmake for the later levels in particular. The matchmaking is fast, which is great, but only the host is capable of starting the game - at least half of the time, the host is afk for a minute or more, which can be very frustrating.

These issues aside, the game IS fun. Shooting zombies feels good. I find the manual reloading a little finicky, especially for shotguns, but it feels satisfying to load your guns up on your own. To name a game to compare this one to, I would have to arbitrarily mention Left 4 Dead - there are obvious differences between the two, but they play similarly. This game's "special infected" are... a little lacking? There's a tanky one that explodes, a tanky one that runs after you, a VERY tanky boss one, and a tanky one that follows you around very slowly and oneshots you. They're all... fine, but not particularly interesting. 

The levels themselves are alright, nothing to write home about - they all follow a more or less identical structure with little to no variation, with the exception of one level. Unless the final encounters are random and I just got very unlucky.

Also, the game runs pretty poorly. I'm on a 2080 Super and a Ryzen 3600 and it was not running well. It improved when I turned off shadows, reduced the texture resolution and reduced enemy ragdoll tendencies. Even then, it would occasionally stutter a bit.

A reasonably fun and interesting game, weapon customization seems interesting, controls make me want to vomit, weapon handling seems inconsistent and at times make me want to smash my controllers.

So the Zombie horde shooting aspect of the game is reasonably quite fun, love me a classic zombie shooter.
However any special infected for whatever reason just 1-shot you all the time no matter what? Which seems like a gross oversight. I played by myself with AI team-mates, and while they were competent enough most of the time, they could not save me from a Juggernaut grab to save their lives, or mine for that matter. This compounded by the fact that the movement is super clunky as the controls can never seem to remember if you're sprinting or not, so sometimes you go to sprint away from or out of the way of a Juggernaut charge, but you slow-walk instead and just get grabbed/killed. Same issue with the Smasher's. All their attacks 1-shot and when the game randomly forces you to walk, it's just a death sentence.
And the controls, as another review put it, it's like the developers looked at all the advancements in VR technology, controls, and control schemes since Arizona Sunshine and just decided to ignore it all. Why? I have no earthly clue, but gross incompetence is my best guess. For starters, holding any object requires you to (playing on Gen1 Vive with Vive wands) hold the grip buttons down at all times to maintain grip on anything except guns (which is a miracle). With one exception being if you're using your off-hand to grab your current weapon (handguns and long-guns), as soon as you let go of the grip button, your hand jumps off the gun. This is especially annoying when using long-guns as you have to keep constant pressure on that grip-button to even be allowed to continue holding the gun, let alone hold it steady. Pistols are less noticeable as most can be wielded with ease using only 1 hand.
Reloading is a fucking nightmare too. It's as though nobody on the dev team has ever held or reloaded a firearm or magazine in their life. The grip angle for the mag is the most inhuman thing I've seen in my life, and actually getting it into the gun is clunky as all hell. Also while not entirely awful, the grip angle on handguns can be slightly better, it's just a little too high.
Suffice to say, with all these awkward and un-ergonomic controls and control methodology, this game is severely taxing on your arms and fingers to play even for short periods of time.
Additionally in regards to weapon handling or lack thereof.
I am an exceptionally good shot in VR, and despite my issues with the controls in this game I was still able to make reasonably consistent shots for the most part. However on occasion I noticed 1 shot would go wide of where I was aiming for seemingly no reason. While not an immense issue one way or the other, it did make it quite frustrating when trying to clear a small group of enemies.

At the end of it all, the game itself is reasonably fun for the short period of time before the fatigue sets in, but as far as VR shooters go, I'll stick with H3VR, which is somehow still leagues ahead of any modern titles in terms of VR guns.

I wanted to like this because L4D in VR sounds amazing, but the implementation just isn't there. It's jank, and not the fun kind of jank.

The biggest problem by far is actually finding a party as there's no guarantee anyone will even be playing at any given time, let alone on the same difficulty and map you selected. The matchmaking similarly doesn't help matters as there is no way to queue for a general difficulty setting; you have to select specific maps, and when you select multiple maps to search for a party in the game will pick one at random rather than make a generalised search for any party on any of those maps. There is also no separation between people searching for a Mutated run on a map that is currently open for that run and people searching for a normal game - which leads to problems when most Mutated runs are excessively difficult unless you're already completely kitted out. This leads to the best solution being to join the studio Discord server to ask for games there, and in my opinion having to rely on an external tool to do basic matchmaking is inexcusable.

All the other problems mostly follow on from that, with uneven difficulty scaling above Veteran, the AI party members being unforgivably dumb (constantly walking in to your line of fire to block your shots, standing in one place and allowing the snowbreed to kill them, poorly kiting around specials and being completely useless for the big Smasher at the end of a run), various bugs in the level geometry that can make items irretrievable, other bugs in the level geometry that lets items sink under the terrain in a way that you can still pick up but can't see, small annoyances like getting stuck on level geometry and dying as a result (And no checkpoints so you go right back to the start of any run if your party wipes, no restarting from the last safe room), and the various dumb bugs that have gone unfixed like a particular mod for the auto shotgun giving it essentially infinite ammo.

The last much more subjective gripe is how the game is designed around an automatic reload system. You press a button to eject the magazine, then bring the weapon to your chest and the game does the rest of the reloading for you. I suppose it's fine on its own, but it makes the gunplay deeply unsatisfying. And while the game does have a manual reload option (called 'advanced reload') that gives you a 50% damage boost, that has its own issues where the game can take a few frames to register you've either initiated or released your grip on parts of the firearm, leading to jank like accidentally un-cocking the SMG or Tommy Gun because those weapons fire from an open bolt, and the game sometimes doesn't realise you let go of the bolt soon enough to stop your character's hand from moving the bolt forward again. To say nothing of how the community generally agrees that you actively detriment your party (when you can find one) if you use the advanced reload on Nightmare or Horror.

Many game-breaking bugs and in-game incentives that ruin the fun. Gameplay loop involves running the same 5 missions repeatedly, trying to get weapon attachments or challenge skins. Which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but there are too many reasons why their gameplay loop is not enjoyable.

Here are the primary reasons for not recommending. Note that most of the pros listed below are barely positive:
[h1] Pros [/h1]
- Gunplay feels okay, defo not the best but decent for a zombie shooter.
- Upgrade system is [b] mostly [/b] for convenience, which means new players would not be at a massive disadvantage due to missing attachments.
- Harvest is easy to come by, so it's easy to tinker with and try out different weapons.
- Voice acting is not awful.
- Music is pretty good.

[h1] Cons [/h1]
- Shooting while strafing with smg is too strong, means that as long as you can kite the zombies (snowbreed, whatever) near ammo, you do not need to strategize. At that point, killing them isn't a challenge, just time consuming.
- Many high-value challenges, especially the Nightmare challenges disincentivize teamwork, because it means you are fighting against your teammates to get enough kills in a given run if you want the skins.
- Quick reload is an inherent advantage over Advanced reload, and the Harvest bonus for Advanced reload does not mean anything since it does not make the mission easier. Most players using Quick reload will end up getting more Harvest anyways due to their advantages with up-time/DPS and versatility.
- Weapon attachment rewards being completely randomized, whether a duplicate or not, is frustrating and artificial padding to keep end-game people playing longer.
- AI pathing is frequently laughable. It is common to see zombies zig-zagging back and forth, slowly inching forward. This is especially noticeable on higher difficulties, which means they are moving faster, messing with their pathing even more.
- Peeker's advantage in the PvP mode is absolutely horrendous. Basically unplayable. Not an issue in harvest runs since the zombies don't have the same problem, though there is still plenty of desync, connection issues, and other issues in online runs.

[h1] Bugs/Bad Features [/h1]
- Using Index controllers, you are unable to hold weapons while simultaneously grabbing items or reloading. This puts players using Index controllers at an inherent disadvantage compared to Quest players.
- Door clipping still nullifies final stands, can skip them entirely and just finish the missions without fighting the last hordes of enemies. Obviously you don't need to, but when the alternative is mindlessly running in circles with your smg and unlimited ammo, you don't really feel like you're missing out on anything.
- You can still sequence break, as in if someone stays near the beginning of a checkpoint and there are gaps or jumps, you can never fail because most zombies will kill themselves (Including elites/bosses) when they realize they cannot get to where you are. Other sequence breaks where the zombies can still path to you mean that you can hold out in more advantageous positions than you otherwise would be able to. Takes more time, but guarantees success, which means it is currently one of the easiest Nightmare strategies.
- You still cannot reload your missile launcher at safe rooms.

This does not include inventory-wiping bugs and other network related issues. I also never addressed issues with bots since they did not massively impact my experience.

Needs a LOT of work to make the experience remotely engaging and cooperative. Even without the bugs and pathing issues, elements such as weapon balance, circle-strafing, and end-game rewards are still huge problems that would need to get addressed.

I was ecstatic for this game to release. I got all of my friend to buy it and those that didn't buy it...i bought it for them. Well now, it's the embarrassing elephant in all our game libraries and here is why. Fun game but I find that when I play it, i just want to re-download and replay AZS...which was a much more complete experience. This feels like a very early access game waiting for direction and inspiration...out of 10, here are the ranks and explanations for a few different things:

Looks/Sounds/Feel --- 7/10 Guns sound great and really feel fun to shoot. Graphics do great across platform and a variety of hardware. It's beyond bland after that...All the enemies are the same, all the levels are nice looking but feel the same and inspire little to no looking around because with the blizzard or dark rooms, you are really just looking at foggy nothingness...

Game play --- 5/10 it's awesome when you first jump in. It's fun when you play through the first time with friends. Feels good the first time you use each weapon. Gets repetitive FAST. Never get a craving to jump back in. 

Variety --- 1/10 very few levels, all play exactly the same, same bosses, same mini bosses...same mission...go, kill, remember to spend an extra 45 seconds running around the room after you cleared it to manually pick up all the essence...

Bugs --- 4/10 most bugs were livable, however, they have a ton of bugs that make it so that you can only progress the game if you play solo for about half of my peer group. Playing solo is the opposite of what this game was designed for, so much so you get AI bots forced on you if you try...but we had to split up and play separately for everyone to progress the map and achieve store goals. There is a bug specifically for Index where you force drop everything you are not actively squeezing. This was not an issue when using quest 2 or vive. They have yet to fix this issue.

Looting/Unlocks/Crafting --- 2/10 You unlock everything in an hour and all crafting is beyond vanilla. All weapons basically have the same attachments, doing the same thing and they are all very nominal stat increases that are not exciting, don't change how the guns feel, sound or play. There is rarity to each crafting attachment that is effectively a slightly stronger stat boots, nothing more. I feel like with how much they leaned into the variety of this game...6 guns with the same handful of generic attachment and 5 levels and 1 mission is not doing it for me...the only thing really worth grinding for is camo...maybe...?

- anyway, really hoping the rest of the game comes out, they fix the bugs, and they add in variety as well as quality of life elements. This game is very much a early access proof of concept for VR in general game. Seriously lacking in any depth, variety  or replay-ability, however, there is so much potential and with the right free updates...it could even be a real game some day. One I am no longer embarrassed to remind my friends I made them buy it.

This game has a lot of small issues that together make it very painful to play. The gameplay itself is a lot of fun, but that just makes the issues more frustrating.

1. Performance is very spotty. I have a 2700 Super and a i5 10400, and even playing on "low" I frequently have  moments when the game completely stops rendering for a second or so when there is a lot going on. Any time there are a lot of zombies, interacting with your gun becomes unreliable, and sometimes my gun floats away for a couple of feet before snapping back. It's not a tracking issue or general issue with my machine, because I've never had any of these problems in Onward, Contractors, Pavlov, etc.

2. Speaking of weapon handling, it's extremely frustrating that there's no option (that I can find) to use your trigger to pull back the charging handle. The detection of where you want to grab is very wonky, and you'll often end up just grabbing your gun when you want to chamber a round. It gets worse when performance drops, which is of course the worst possible time.

3. The AI is basically worthless. Playing with 3 bots is almost as much use as playing with one human who has never played a VR game before. They mostly just get in your  way by blocking doorways, and then complain about you shooting them. The only useful thing they do is revive you, but you've only got about a 20% chance that they'll choose to do that instead of running around failing to kill zombies.

4. Speaking of the terrible writing, every time you do a mission, you get all of the "story" voice acting all over again. If there's any difference in the script each time, it's very minor. The worst is at the end of the "Relay" mission, when you have to sit there listening to them wrap up the story long after you've finished killing the zombies. Also, the AI's only have a handful of voice lines, and repeat them endlessly. My favorite one is the guy who says "You're afraid of the dark, Mal?" despite the fact that there's no character named Mal and no one else has said anything to prompt it.

5. When you start the game or end a mission, you're dropped into a closet that you have to leave to enter the lobby. You can't tweak your weapons (or even see what you have equipped) in the lobby, so you have to run across the lobby to a separate room. If they are going to insist on making you enter a special loadout room, it would be nice if it wasn't literally the farthest point away from where you spawn.

6. Moving things around in the loadout room is very unintuitive. Instead of grabbing things with your hand or laying them down, everything is based on what direction your hand is "pointed". That means you'll often pick up the wrong thing, or drop something in the wrong spot. It's also a headache grabbing your holstered weapons if there's a grenade or gun laying on the ground at your feet, as it will usually try to pick that up instead.

7. Grenades / health / pickups are stored in your wrist like in HL: Alyx. The problem is that the items stored on your wrists are only illuminated by the environment. So if you're in a dark room (which is 80% of the rooms), you won't be able to see if you have a grenade stored in your wrist or not.

I'm sure I could keep going until I hit the character limit, but no one is going to read this far anyway. The game is fun but it needs a couple dozen tweaks to make it not infuriating. I usually start out excited to play, and end up annoyed.

This is a really fun game for an arcade VR shooter, and I have had a good amount of fun with it, which is why I'm sad to give it a negative review. Why? The biggest reason is that not very many people play this game. It does have crossplay with PlayStation, but even with that, it can be difficult or even impossible to find a game to play. According to Steam charts, this game has a hard time getting 70 people to play, and I can't imagine it's any different on PlayStation.

Another crippling factor is that even when you do find a squad of players, there is a very good chance that someone will lose connection while the match is starting or have atrocious lag. On higher difficulties (since that is all anyone ever plays), this is a death sentence, and you might as well leave and try to get a full squad. The loss of that one player and their firepower is enough to tip the scales against you, even if the rest of you are armed to the teeth with the best equipment in the game.

I also want to touch on progression, as this game's progression is very grindy. Since people only play on the hardest difficulties and you are just starting out, you will be next to, if not entirely, useless until you unlock the things you need to be useful. Even with the time I have put into the game, I am not at the point where I am useful to my max-level teammates. The only silver lining to this is that sometimes veteran players will take pity on you and give you one of their max-upgraded guns, but don't go into the game expecting this. It's only happened once to me, and for them to rebuild it for themselves is a significant resource investment and something they might not want to do for a random player.

I also don't think any of these issues are going to be fixed since Vertigo Games is going to be making "Metro Awakening." It's safe to assume that all the devs who worked on this game have moved to this new project, which is very disappointing as I had hoped this game would have a longer lifespan.

A very awesome VR "Left 4 Dead" alike. Changed just enough to make some fresh new mechanics that up play-ability over L4D, IMO. The sad thing is, the difficulty is very, VERY much too hard. This is in single player, and it doesn't get much better for two players. The higher difficulties are a raging inferno of mass runs of zombies that overwhelm, and bosses that eradicate.

You NEED the better gear to play higher difficulties, and you can't get it without playing them! This chicken and egg dilemma really lowers the replay-ability.

The game mechanics are pretty decent for a Left 4 Dead style VR shooter, and the optimization is pretty decent. The shooting feels nice and aiming is purposefully a little sluggish to help you stabilize shots (it's hard to explain, but it's almost like trying to aim underwater a little bit. It isn't tedious and actually helps against the jitter often seen in these VR shooters. This is a big positive). It's also one of the few games where when I throw an item, it actually goes where I intended it to go, another common issue in VR games. Returning from launch, a couple of things have changed since launch. a handful of guns were added, the grind eased up a little bit (it's still an extremely grindy and luck-dependant game, just not as much anymore), manual reloading has been improved but is still finicky and forces you to often crash your VERY expensive controllers together every so often, and horde mode was added along with one new mission and mutations to old missions that change daily.

There are still many issues, however. The AI bots are still completely worthless, won't pick up items, can't aim, and will actively protect zombies by constantly blocking your shots. Remember to mute NPC voices in your setting to protect your sanity against the AI constantly complaining their face is blocking your bullets. Because of this, you'll be subject to the games community, which is a hit or miss. There are some people who will help you along the way you'll have a great time, but most of the time people will hotmic shitty music, be on the phone, complain, pester, whine, scream, bicker, refuse to communicate, run off on their own to die, try to command your every action, and/or will not speak English. This isn't much of a fault of the game developers but god damn does it ruin the experience. Gun stats and upgrades are often extremely vague and true values hidden in patch notes, which isn't very helpful when you're trying to modify your guns to suit your needs and it's extremely frustrating when the game refuses to give you upgrades for your favorite gun, while you've managed to unlock everything for a gun you never want to use. The content in the game also gets old very quickly, and the devs seem to have a very slow pace adding new ones.

Overall, this game, even after all of the updates in the last couple of months, is STILL not even close to being worth 40 bucks. If you're someone who's fortunate enough to have 3 other friends who often play VR games and are also willing to play this game, I can see this game being an absolute blast. Unfortunately, if you're like me who's only got one friend like that, and have to choose between the horrible AI or horrible people, this game is a hard pass.

[h1] A Very Solid VR Experience That Feels Unfinished [/h1]

The game has a great foundation, super solid gunplay with good dual wielding implementation and simple yet fun gameplay, graphics are good for the most part with an atmospheric feel and the weapon customisation is very well done, headshots are satisfying, the difficulties feel very well balanced overall, floppy disks are a great way to do unlocks and the sound design is fantastic. A genuinely brilliant VR game, but only for a few hours.


Unfortunately that's where my praise for the game ends. the foundation isn't built on. There's only 5 levels currently, with 2 of them being particularly short and one being a gimmicky final level, very little changes on replays and the only thing to aim for is weapon modifications. The game peaks in it's first level and I blame this on the games biggest flaw; a lack of variety, with only 6 weapons, a handful of enemy types, one reused boss and little change in where you fight enemies (overall themes are different but it just boils down to large empty spaces, the game gets stale. Fast. There is also the PvP but it's weak and not popular enough to regularly find full lobbies. Enemies don't really take into account your hitboxes with attacks and moreso just hit unless you interrupt their clunky animations. I understand why this is the case but it still feels dirty when you get hit by it, not to mention it completely breaks immersion.

The game is also littered with QoL issues and bugs, the party system is dreadful, manual grip doesnt let you swap guns from holsters, enabling hand swapping prioritises grabbing guns over ammo so you end up having trouble reloading, the shotgun feels uncomfortably short, the black screen whenever you SLIGHTLY clip with something is infuriating and completely breaks immersion, the jump downs are done poorly, you either instantly transition down, or put on the more immersive option and risk clipping out of bounds. Guns disappear for no real reason, the MT-47 bolt occasionally has a misplaced hitbox, doors can just be walked through, the one NPC in the game that you regularly see can become unresponsive and stop you progressing the game until you leave and come back, the shooting range refuses to give new guns ammo until you reload the area, the A.I. (as well as being completely stupid) gets buggy dealing with being frozen, corpses regularly get stuck in walls and ceilings, multiple spots where world boundaries/flat textures can be seen, I could go on but you get the idea.

The game has a lot of potential, like a hell of a lot, but it feels like an early access game, or a proof of concept, but considering that these are the guys who made arizona sunshine, and we're far enough into VR where that isn't needed in this capacity AND it's a whopping 30 quid, that's not even close to being worth the money. It ends too quick, there's not enough variety in anything in the game and it needs a lot of tweaking. 

I know the developers have a long roadmap for the game and plan on a lot of updates but come on. This is genuinely pitiful for a game that costs so much, with that price, it has to compete with games like Pavlov, Beat Saber, Blade and Sorcery, Saints and Sinners etc. and it doesn't come close to comparing. 

I really enjoyed my time with this game, truly, but now I'm just craving more, which the game doesn't provide, it's really good with friends despite the awful party system and could go on to become one of the better VR titles available, it just needs to be much more fleshed out. I look forward to seeing where this game goes but unfortunately, at it's current price, and the state that it's in, I just can't recommend it.

The reason I wouldn't recommend this game is that this game has been out for two years but it feels like it still isn't fully developed yet. There are TONS of bugs, many will cause you to lose the last minutes or hours of your life because you lose any rewards you've earned when certain bugs hit you. Also, their party system is still almost non existent so good luck looking for a group to play with. I often load up the the game, check for any parties looking another player and then leave feeling like no one is playing.
Their party system is really bad. The majority of the game is you going on runs to collect rewards and work towards improving your customized weapons. However, the runs must be run with 4 people and the game will fill out the party with computer controlled characters if your party is missing people. The problem with this is that computer controlled characters are very weak and won't work well in the higher difficulty. The game has no way to actually see who's looking for a party or has a party looking for more players. 
Here's how the party system works, you chose your play mode, level and your difficulty and you tell the game you're ready. If someone else did this before you with the same difficulty, then you'll join their party. If there's no one else, then you create an empty party and you can wait or continue with computer controlled characters. Because there's so many difficulties, levels, and play modes, you end up creating a party over and over in each possible combination that you want to play. You can see people in the "lobby" and invite them to join but what often happens is that the person invited is not a fit for the run you want to do; for example, I was running a very high level run in a very hard mode and two of the people in the party were very inexperienced and under equipped. This actually happens often and the other players usually carry the team. 
Finally, the game feels neglected. Bugs are around for months if not years and features like a good party system seem like a pipe dream. This game has been out for two years now but it feels like a 3-6 month old game. This game feels like it has a lot of potential until you realize it's a two+ year old game, then it feels neglected.

Here's an example of a bug that should have been fixed immediately: In Sep 2022, they released a update that caused one of the guns to become extremely over powered. I’m not sure I’ve ever been so split about a game. I really want to love ATF but it’s got just enough issues to make me hesitant about recommending it to others. 

First of all though, the Pros:
- If you’re a fan of intense co-op shooters with a pretty steep difficulty curve this could be one for you. To master the higher difficulties and unlock the best weapons and mods you need to learn how different weapons excel in different situations, how to utilise throwables and wrist devices to their full potential and how to move quickly but safely through the missions. If you have a group of friends who enjoy a challenge then I think you will enjoy the moment to moment gameplay of ATF.

- There are regular updates to the game, both to fix bugs and exploits and to add new content and QoL improvements. 

- Cross-platform support is very clean and easy. Steam users can team up with Quest users and Oculus users with a simple party invite.

- You can choose between quick reloading (slapping the gun against your chest) or active (realistic) reloading. You get a significant damage bonus doing active reloading which I like a lot. Unfortunately quick reloading is undoubtedly the superior choice until you can get extended magazines from higher difficulties. 

Now the unfortunate Cons:
- There are some game-breaking bugs here. They are infrequent but if you’re unlucky, as I was, you can end up in situations where someone will get stuck in a wall or the floor which can mean the end of a run. Switching from smooth movement to teleport sometimes fixes this but other times the person stuck couldn’t access their menu to change this option. This is infuriating when it happens towards the end of a hard mission. If you fail missions in ATF you lose any unlockables you may have picked up, which is understandable, but it means that bugs like these need to be removed otherwise you’ve just wasted your time. 
Other bugs include enemies getting stuck in walls. Enemies that need to be cleared in order to be able to progress to the next area, so you end up running around spraying up the walls hoping to clip them so you can continue. 

- After passing a certain point the progression system is heavily weighted in favour of having a full team of 4 players to clear the higher difficulties. If you want to try it with fewer actual players (I have no interest in playing with randoms) you kind of need the weapon modifications that you can only get from those difficulties, so you end up in this awkward situation where the difficulty becomes a brick wall almost. I will admit the challenge of this can be exciting but then someone gets stuck in a wall and you wonder why you bother with this game at all. 

- If you’re here for story or immersion I would advise that you give this one a miss. The story is wafer thin and the world feels somewhat empty and uninteresting most of the time. I get why that is, the game can create hordes of enemies to send at you which looks amazing and the engine can only do so much, but I never felt immersed or impressed by the world. 

- You get bombarded with party invites from randoms in the hub. 

ATF doesn’t have tons of replayability for me. It’s a game I come back to occasionally to see what’s new and I usually have a good time whenever I do. However, due to some of the bugs that are still present I can’t recommend it unfortunately.

I set out to play through this VR rip-off of Left4Dead solo and then replay it online at harder difficulties once I had learned the basics.

Halfway through (3 of the 5 maps), I felt pretty certain that I would end up giving this short and unpolished game a slightly reserved but positive recommendation.

Then, as the zombie count increased, the frames started dropping. Even though sub-90fps in VR can be quite jarring, it's something I've learned to tolerate. But here, it seemed to go hand in hand with nasty glitches. Suddenly, the manual gun reload became super unreliable and inconsistent. The weapon model would start to drift out of position and remain there, something I never experience in any other similar VR FPS games.

I have an Intel 8700K CPU (@4.8ghz) and a RTX 3080 GPU. Regardless of the quality preset, this would happen. I double-checked that there was no thermal throttling going on.

There's potential here, but I cannot recommend it in its current state, and I have no intention of spending more time with it.
